title: How to Swim Freestyle: A Complete Beginner's Guide
description: Covers body position, arm pull, breathing rhythm, and kicking technique for front crawl. Great starting point for anyone learning freestyle from scratch.

title: Breaststroke Technique Breakdown
description: Step-by-step explanation of the breaststroke pull, kick, and glide cycle, with common mistakes to avoid.

title: Backstroke Tips for Beginners
description: Learn the fundamentals of backstroke: arm recovery, head position, and how to stay straight without being able to see where you're going.

title: Water Safety Rules Everyone Should Know
description: Essential safety rules for pools, lakes, and open water — including never swimming alone, understanding currents, and what to do if you get into trouble.

title: Understanding Rip Currents
description: How to spot a rip current, what to do if you're caught in one, and how to help others safely. Critical reading for anyone swimming in the ocean.

title: Child Water Safety: What Parents Need to Know
description: A practical guide to keeping children safe in and around water, covering supervision, barriers, and teaching early water skills.

title: Breathing Technique for Swimmers
description: Why breathing is the hardest part of swimming for most beginners, and how to practice bilateral breathing, exhaling underwater, and timing your breath with your stroke.

title: Bubble Drills for New Swimmers
description: Simple drills to get comfortable exhaling underwater — a foundational skill that everything else in swimming is built on.

title: How to Stop Swallowing Water When You Swim
description: Common reasons swimmers inhale water and practical techniques to breathe more cleanly during freestyle and other strokes.

title: Beginner Swim Workout Plans
description: Three sample swim workouts for beginners — designed to build endurance gradually without overwhelming someone just learning to swim laps.

title: How to Structure a Swim Practice
description: Explains warm-up, main set, and cool-down structure, with guidance on how to pace yourself and track progress over time.

title: Using Swim Equipment: Fins, Paddles, and Kickboards
description: A guide to common training tools, when to use them, and what each one helps you develop — useful for swimmers ready to add variety to their practice.
